---
title: Rules
---

Rules report problems in a BibTeX project.
Run `biblint rule` to list the rules in the installed binary, or `biblint rule duplicate_key` for one rule's summary and fix status.

## Rule reference

| Rule | Default | Fix             | Purpose                                                                  |
| ---- | :-----: | :-------------: | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `syntax_error`  | yes     | none            | BibTeX syntax is incomplete or unbalanced.                               |
| `formatting`  | yes     | safe/configured | The file is not in the selected canonical format.                        |
| `missing_key`  | yes     | none            | An entry has no citation key.                                            |
| `key_format`  | no      | none            | An existing key differs from the configured generated key.               |
| `duplicate_key`  | yes     | none            | A citation key is used more than once.                                   |
| `duplicate_doi`  | no      | none            | Two entries share a DOI.                                                 |
| `duplicate_citation`  | no      | none            | Two entries share a normalized author/title/number citation fingerprint. |
| `duplicate_abstract`  | no      | none            | Two entries share the first 100 normalized abstract characters.          |
| `duplicate_field` | yes     | none            | An entry repeats a field name.                                           |
| `empty_field` | yes     | none            | A field has no value.                                                    |
| `unsupported_escape` | yes     | none            | A character has no built-in LaTeX escape.                                |
| `unsupported_construct` | yes     | none            | Source was preserved because biblint could not structure it.             |

`syntax_error` diagnostics have error severity.
Most structural problems are warnings.
Unsupported escapes and preserved source are notes because biblint has kept the original content intact.

## Selecting rules

```toml
[lint]
select = ["duplicate_key"]
extend-select = ["key_format", "duplicate_doi"]
ignore = ["unsupported_escape"]
```

`select` replaces the default-enabled set.
`extend-select` adds rules to it, and `ignore` always wins.
Use `all` as a wildcard.
Per-file exceptions use the same names:

```toml
[lint.per-file-ignores]
"generated/**" = ["formatting", "unsupported_construct"]
```

## Project-level checks

When checking a directory or multiple files, biblint also compares entries across files.
This catches repeated keys and enabled DOI, citation, or abstract fingerprints that a single-file check cannot see.
Diagnostics include a related location for the first occurrence.

The optional duplicate rules are disabled by default because DOI, citation, and abstract matches need a judgment about whether two records are actually the same work.
Enable only the comparisons useful for the project.

## Key-format checks

`key_format` is disabled by default because changing a citation key can break references elsewhere.
Enable it explicitly:

```toml
[lint]
extend-select = ["key_format"]

[lint.key-format]
style = "better-bibtex"
```

The rule reports a suggested key but does not attach an automatic rename fix.
The configured formula and the key-generation transform share one evaluator; see [Citekey generation](key-generation.md) for the compatibility boundary.
